title: codeanalyzer canonical v2 analysis output
description: The canonical CLDK analysis schema (v2): the invariant spine every codeanalyzer emits and every SDK consumes. One additive containment tree (application -> module -> type -> callable -> body) with typed edge overlays (call_graph, cfg, cdg, ddg, summary, param_in, param_out). This document is PERMISSIVE by construction: it states what must be present and what a shared field means, and leaves every node open so a language may add its own fields. The per-language schemas under v2/json/<lang>/ $ref these definitions and close them with `unevaluatedProperties: false`, so a field an analyzer emits but nobody recorded fails validation there rather than here. Levels: L1 tree + call sites, L2 callee refinement + call_graph, L3 full body + cfg/cdg/ddg, L4 synthetic param vertices + param_in/param_out/summary. Absence means 'no fact'; the only sanctioned null is a call node's `callee` before L2.

x-cldk.note: Derived from the three analyzer model sources named above and cross-checked against real output of each analyzer at its released version (the *.sample.json files beside the per-language schemas). Where the three disagree, the canonical schema states the intersection and the disagreement is recorded under x-cldk.divergences rather than papered over.
divergences: import: java names the imported path `path`; python and typescript name it `module`.
decorator arguments: java emits `args` (flat list); python and typescript emit `positional_arguments` + `keyword_arguments`.
leaf positions: java gives comments/imports/parameters/decorators a `span`; python and typescript give them flat start_line/start_column/end_line/end_column.
span offsets: java and python `span.bytes` are UTF-8 byte offsets; typescript `span.bytes` are UTF-16 char offsets into module.source.
span columns: java and typescript columns are 1-based; python columns are 0-based (ast semantics), lines are 1-based everywhere.
module node: python has no `span` and adds `file_path`/`module_name`; java and typescript carry `span` and key identity off the symbol_table key.
module cache metadata: python emits `last_modified` and `file_size` on the wire; typescript strips them (keeping `content_hash`); java emits `content_hash` only.
external_symbols values: python and typescript emit {id, kind, module, name}; java emits {kind, signature, declaring_type} and leaves the id to the map key.
unresolved config reads: python calls the list `config_reads_unresolved`; typescript calls it `config_reads`; java emits neither (it emits config keys under artifacts only).
ddg L3 provenance token: java tags syntactic edges `ssa`, typescript tags them `reaching-defs`, python emits both tokens.
callee refinement slot: typescript writes `callee: null` on an unresolved call node; java and python omit the key.
envelope k_limit: python and typescript emit it at L3+; java has no such field.
python-only application sections: `repository`, `entrypoint_report`, `unresolved_imports` are emitted by python (typescript emits `unresolved_imports` too, java neither).

schema_version.description: Version of this canonical schema line. All three analyzers ship 2.0.0.

language.description: The analyzed language; also the `<lang>` segment of every can:// id.

max_level.description: Highest analysis level populated. Consumers read this rather than sniffing for keys.

k_limit.description: Access-path depth bound of the L3/L4 dataflow. Present at L3+ on the analyzers that bound it.

AnalyzerInfo.description: Which analyzer produced this payload, and how it was configured.

config.description: Analyzer options in effect. Open map; not every analyzer emits it.

Span.description: Where a node lives in source. `start`/`end` are [line, column]; `bytes` are [from, to) offsets into the owning module's `source`, so source[bytes[0]:bytes[1]] reproduces the node's text.

Position.description: [line, column]. Lines are 1-based everywhere; column base is language-specific (see x-cldk.divergences).

Application.description: The root node: the containment tree plus the application-scope edge overlays. Every id in every edge list must resolve to a node reachable from here (no dangling endpoints).

name.description: The resolved application name the id is built from: a non-blank --app-name, else the input directory's basename. Optional until codeanalyzer-java and codeanalyzer-python emit it, then required (codellm-devkit/.github#93).

symbol_table.description: Per-file analysis, keyed by repo-relative POSIX path (no absolute paths, no '..').

call_graph.description: L2. Callable -> callable edges, endpoints are can:// ids.

external_symbols.description: L2. Id homes for call-graph endpoints outside the project, keyed by their @external id.

param_in.description: L4. actual_in -> formal_in, endpoints are global ordinal ids.

param_out.description: L4. formal_out -> actual_out, endpoints are global ordinal ids.

artifacts.description: The repository-artifact layer: recognized non-code files, keyed by repo-relative path. Level-free (identical at every -a level).

dependencies.description: Declared third-party dependencies, evidence-tagged via `prov`. Level-free.

unresolved_imports.description: Imports no declared dependency accounts for (the dependency-hygiene signal).

config_uses.description: Resolved config reads: a recognized read joined to the ConfigKey it names.

Module.description: One source file / compilation unit. Holds the file's text once; every node's text is a slice of it.

source.description: The whole file's text, stored once.

content_hash.description: Hash of `source`, for incremental caching and per-module diffing in the Neo4j push. Not identity.

types.description: Top-level types declared in this file, keyed by name.

functions.description: Module-level callables, keyed by signature. Absent or empty for class-only languages.

Type.description: A type node. `kind` is the specific type kind (class | struct | interface | enum | record | trait | type_alias | namespace | ...), never a pile of is_* booleans.

callables.description: Methods and constructors, keyed by signature.

fields.description: Declared fields / attributes / enum members, keyed by name.

types.description: Member / inner types, keyed by name. Nesting is encoded by this containment position.

Callable.description: A function, method, constructor, accessor or lambda. `span.bytes` slices the whole declaration out of module.source; it is present for every callable the source declares and absent only on a compiler-synthesized member (e.g. java's implicit default constructor, discovered at L2).

signature.description: Human-readable signature; the last path segment of `id`, from the one signatureOf().

body.description: L1 holds the call nodes; L3 completes it with the rest of the statements. Keyed by local ordinal id (`line:col`, or `@tag` for a synthetic vertex).

callables.description: Nested callables (closures / local functions), keyed by signature.

cfg.description: L3. Control-flow edges over this callable's body nodes.

ddg.description: L3 (syntactic) widened at L4 (alias-aware). Data-dependence edges.

summary.description: L4. actual_in -> actual_out transitive intra-caller shortcuts.

BodyNode.description: A node inside a callable's `body`: an AST region (statement | call | return | branch | loop | switch) or a synthetic analysis vertex (entry | exit | formal_in | formal_out | actual_in | actual_out). The map key is its local id, so a body node carries no `id` of its own.

id.description: The GLOBAL ordinal id of this body node: `<callable-id>@<local>`, the same value the Neo4j projection merges its body-node label on. Optional on the spine only because an analyzer may not have adopted it yet; a language that emits it requires it (codeanalyzer-python#176).

callee.description: call nodes only: the callee's id. The one sanctioned refinement slot - absent (or null) at L1, an id from L2 on.

of.description: Synthetic param vertices: the value this vertex stands for (a parameter name, `argN`, `$ret`).

parent.description: actual_in / actual_out: the local id of the call site the vertex belongs to.

Field.description: A declared binding: a module-level variable, a class attribute / interface property, or an enum member.

Parameter.description: One declared parameter, in declaration order.

id.description: `<callable-id>@formal_in:<i>` for this parameter's position: the L4 formal_in vertex that carries it. A forward reference below level 4 - the vertex it names does not exist in `body` until `-a 4` (codeanalyzer-python#176).

Import.description: One import declaration. The imported path is `path` in java and `module` in python/typescript (see x-cldk.divergences).

Decorator.description: One decorator / annotation application, structured rather than a source string. Argument capture differs per language (see x-cldk.divergences).

IdEdge.description: The bare edge shape: two node ids and nothing else. The list name IS the edge type, so there is no `type` field.

ParamEdge.description: A param_in (actual_in -> formal_in) or param_out (formal_out -> actual_out) edge at application scope. `var` is the callee-side formal the edge binds: the parameter name, `$ret` for the return port, or a global's access path on a global read/write. Set on every such edge - a property present on some edges and not others is a three-valued trap for any predicate on it (codeanalyzer-python#195).

CallEdge.description: L2. One call-graph edge, callable -> callable, identity-only.

weight.description: Number of call sites merged into this edge.

CfgEdge.description: L3. One control-flow edge between body nodes of the same callable.

kind.description: fallthrough | true | false | switch_case | loop_back | exception | return | break | continue, plus language additions.

DdgEdge.description: L3 (syntactic) / L4 (alias-aware). One data-dependence edge between body nodes of the same callable.

var.description: The k-limited access path the dependence carries.

ExternalSymbol.description: An id home for a call target outside the analyzed project - an edge endpoint, not a tree node. Keyed by its @external id.

Artifact.description: A recognized non-code file (config, manifest, CI, container spec, data). Ids are language-neutral (can://artifact/<app>/<path>) so sibling-language analyzers land on the same node.

path.description: Repo-relative POSIX path; also the map key.

roles.description: Open vocabulary: dependency-manifest | tool-config | container-image | service-topology | iac | ci | env | packaging | legal | docs | script | unknown.

source.description: The whole file's text when captured, else "" - never a prefix.

ConfigKey.description: One configuration key flattened out of a config-bearing artifact. Contained by its artifact; containment mirrors the DEFINES_CONFIG relationship in the graph projection.

key.description: Dotted path; numeric segments for arrays (services.web.ports.0).

references.description: Recognized ${VAR}/$VAR tokens, deduplicated, in order of appearance.

Dependency.description: One declared third-party dependency (or a lockfile-only transitive pin).

kind.description: runtime | dev | optional | build, plus language additions (npm `peer`).

declared_in.description: Id of the Artifact that declares it.

ImportBinding.description: A top-level import no declared dependency accounts for.

ConfigUseEdge.description: One resolved config read: a recognized read whose key closed on exactly one literal matching a declared ConfigKey. `src` is the read's global ordinal id, `dst` the ConfigKey id.

ConfigRead.description: A recognized config read that resolved to no declared key - first-class, so an untraceable read is as visible as a traced one. This list shrinks as levels rise; it is the one deliberately non-monotonic section.

site.description: Global ordinal id of the read.

EntrypointReport.description: Coverage and failure record for the entrypoint pass. The pass under-approximates by design, so silence is its failure mode: this is what distinguishes 'this application has no entrypoints' from 'the pass found nothing'. Always present once an analyzer runs the pass.

frameworks_detected.description: Frameworks the detector recognized in this application.

unresolved.description: Written spelling -> count, for decorators and base classes the pass could not name.

errors.description: Failures during the pass. The pass is additive: a failure loses flags, never the analysis.

Entrypoint.description: One way a callable or type is invoked from outside the application - a route, a CLI command, a scheduled task. A node may carry several. `confidence` lets a consumer threshold on evidence quality: `declared` (a manifest says so), `certain` (a framework rule matched a resolved name), `heuristic` (the written spelling reads like an entrypoint).

rule.description: A rules.yml `id:`, or an engine name.

via.description: can:// id of the routed node dispatching here.
